title: Record collections and Ed Beach's WRVR collection
summary: They compare record collections and recall the disk jockey Ed Beach's records and money troubles.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: I don't know. I really don't know. And let me say something to you. The largest record collection I ever saw in my life -- one night I was in The Metropole, Red used to clown a lot, he used to say, "Here come Chester Campbell, Jr., bassist from Pennsylvania," And I had a friend of mine, "Carl Shepherd (phonetic spelling) drummer from so-and-so." So we were standing at the bar, talking to this fellow with a southern accent, so we were buying one another drinks. So when Red got finished his set he came down and he said, "Look, I'm going to --" I can't think of the gentleman's name, "he said, "Would you guys like to go --" we went to a town house in the
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
'70s, I saw more records there than I ever saw records -- it was unbelievable.
You have a pretty big record collection,yourself.
Mine? I've got over 2,000 LP's. Now listen to this. What is the name of the gentleman that was on WEVD, no, not WEVD, WRVR, disk jockey.

Ed Beech. Now listen to this -- when Ed Beech, they were getting ready to take him off the air, a friend of mine who is a doctor borrowed $10,000 to buy part of his collection. But he never bought it because people started writing in to keep him on the air. But since then he's gone off. Now, I'll tell you why I didn't take music up professionally. When my father -- after he started growing older and gigging got rough, he said, "Chester, can music," he was going to kill the music industry. A musician makes a date,he gets paid for the date and

That's what seems to be with the President of Local 802.
